title: Review: Human gas exchange and ventilation; Membrane structure (fluid mosaic); Factors affecting membrane permeability; Osmosis and water potential
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MB05#t3 term and clue written for the game; MB03a#t2 term and clue written for the game; MB05#t1 term and clue written for the game; MB05#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EX02b#N.2, MB01a#N.3a, MB01b#N.13, MB03a#N.10, MB05#N.8, EX02b#N.7, MB01a#N.10a, MB03a#N.6a, EX02b#N.15a, MB01a#N.7. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Absorbance
items.clue: Measure of how much light a sample takes up; higher when more pigment is present.

items.label: Crenation
items.clue: Shrinking and puckering of the surface of a cell without a wall as water leaves it.

items.label: Tonoplast
items.clue: Membrane around the vacuole, the first of two that beetroot pigment must cross to leave the cell.

items.label: Calibration curve
items.clue: Graph of readings for known concentrations, used to turn a sample's reading into a concentration.

questions.stem: A student's spirometer readings are: tidal volume 0.5 dm³, inspiratory reserve volume 3.0 dm³, expiratory reserve volume 1.2 dm³. What is the student's vital capacity?

options.text: 4.2 dm³
4.7 dm³
3.5 dm³
1.7 dm³

questions.explanation: Vital capacity = tidal volume + inspiratory reserve + expiratory reserve = 0.5 + 3.0 + 1.2 = 4.7 dm³.

questions.stem: Why do phospholipids form a bilayer when they are mixed with water?

options.text: Enzymes in the cell join the phospholipids together into a sheet, using energy released from ATP.
The whole molecule repels water, so the phospholipids gather away from it as a droplet of oil.
Covalent bonds form between neighbouring phospholipids, linking them into one rigid sheet of molecules.
Hydrophilic heads face the water and hydrophobic tails are shielded from it, so the sheet forms spontaneously.

questions.explanation: In water the most stable arrangement is a continuous sheet two molecules thick, heads towards the water on both sides and tails in the middle. It forms with no energy input.

questions.stem: A student claims that proteins in the plasma membrane can move sideways within the membrane. Which observation would best support this claim?

options.text: As the cell grows, the total amount of protein in its plasma membrane increases steadily.
When fluorescent proteins in one small patch are permanently bleached, the patch glows again within a minute.
Micrographs show proteins scattered among the phospholipids rather than forming a separate layer.
Proteins labelled on the outer surface of the plasma membrane are later found inside the cytosol.

questions.stem: Jam contains so much sugar that most bacteria landing on it cannot grow. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Sugar diffuses into the bacteria until there is enough inside them to poison them.
Water leaves the bacteria by osmosis into the jam, so their cytoplasm shrinks and they cannot grow.
Water enters the bacteria from the jam, so the bacteria swell up and burst.
Their cell walls stop any water from crossing, so the bacteria cannot take in water.

questions.explanation: The jam is far more concentrated than the cytoplasm. Water leaves the cells by osmosis; the contents shrink away from the wall, and without water the cells cannot grow.

questions.stem: A student makes a 1-in-10 dilution series: each step transfers 1.0 cm³ of the previous solution into 9.0 cm³ of distilled water. What is the concentration in the third diluted tube, as a fraction of the stock?
questions.explanation: Each step is 1.0 cm³ in a total of 10.0 cm³: ×1/10. Three steps: (1/10)³ = 1/1000.

questions.stem: During a run, a student's blood carbon dioxide concentration rises, blood pH falls from 7.40 to 7.32 and ventilation rate rises from 12 to 30 breaths per minute. Which statement correctly links these changes?

options.text: The extra carbon dioxide makes the blood more alkaline, as shown by the fall in pH, and chemoreceptors in the brainstem respond to this by increasing ventilation.
Carbon dioxide is a gas and so cannot change pH; the fall in pH is due to lactic acid from the muscles, which is detected by chemoreceptors in the lungs.
Carbon dioxide forms carbonic acid, lowering pH; brainstem chemoreceptors detect this and the medulla increases signals to the breathing muscles.
The student consciously decides to breathe faster on feeling out of breath, and the changes in carbon dioxide and pH are consequences of this, not causes.

questions.stem: A student draws a two-dimensional representation of the fluid mosaic model. Which feature of the drawing is correct?

options.text: The tails of the inner layer point into the cytoplasm, as the cytoplasm is the inside of the cell.
The proteins are drawn at regular, equal spacings, like tiles set in a fixed pattern across the sheet.
Glycoproteins are drawn with their carbohydrate chains on the cytoplasmic side of the membrane.
Cholesterol is drawn among the phospholipids within the bilayer, not on its surface.

questions.explanation: Cholesterol sits within the bilayer among the phospholipids. The hydrophilic heads form both surfaces and the hydrophobic tails form the core.

questions.stem: A strip of onion epidermis is mounted in a concentrated sucrose solution and viewed under a microscope. Which statement describes what happens to its cells?

options.text: Water leaves each cell by osmosis and the whole cell, wall included, shrinks and crumples inward, just as an animal cell crenates.
Water leaves each cell by osmosis, the protoplast shrinks and its membrane pulls away from the wall: the cells are plasmolysed.
Water leaves each cell by osmosis and an empty space forms between the wall and the membrane, because the wall lets nothing through.
Water enters each cell by osmosis, because the concentrated solution is hypotonic to them, and the cells become turgid.

questions.stem: At rest, an athlete's tidal volume is 0.6 dm³, inspiratory reserve volume 2.8 dm³ and expiratory reserve volume 1.4 dm³. During hard exercise her tidal volume rises to 2.2 dm³. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Her vital capacity rises to 6.4 dm³, because the extra tidal volume is added on to her resting volumes.
Her reserve volumes stay at 2.8 and 1.4 dm³, because the reserves are used only in a single maximal breath.
Vital capacity stays 4.8 dm³; the larger breaths leave reserves totalling 2.6 dm³.
The extra air comes from her residual volume, which can be breathed out only during exercise.

questions.stem: Which statement about glycoproteins in the plasma membrane is correct?

options.text: Their carbohydrate is on the extracellular side and is used in cell recognition and adhesion.
Their carbohydrate is on the cytoplasmic side and is respired when the cell lacks glucose.
Their carbohydrate projects from both faces of the membrane so that either face can be recognised.
They are transport proteins whose carbohydrate forms the channel through which sugars enter the cell.

questions.explanation: Glycoproteins are proteins with a carbohydrate chain attached. The carbohydrate faces outwards, where it works in cell recognition and cell adhesion.
